newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHERS SHINE IN RAIN-HIT PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHERS SHINE IN RAIN-HIT PRACTICE.

text.p: Ralf Schumacher of Germany upstaged his older brother and double world champion Michael in Friday's opening practice for Sunday's German Grand Prix but the times meant little as the weather dominated proceedings.
"It's a very nice feeling to be quickest at my home track and we really had to work for it," said Ralf Schumacher, who clocked one minute 46.196 seconds.
"But although I am quite happy, it doesn't count for anything at the end of the day. We should not really take the result because the weather meant other drivers could not improve."
The first session had started with a damp track that quickly dried but the drivers managed only a few quick laps before the rain returned near the end of the hour-long session.
Just before the start of the second session, however, the rain came down much more heavily and flooded parts of the track, meaning the drivers did not venture out for the first 10 minutes.

The conditions eventually improved to leave the track almost dry near the end of the session but the best times were still more than one second slower than Ralf Schumacher's fastest lap of one minute 46.196 seconds from the first session.
The Jordan driver ended his second session in the barriers after a spin at the Ayrton Senna curve.
Michael Schumacher, driving a Ferrari, was second quickest in 1:46.322.
Briton Johnny Herbert was third fastest on 1:46.517.
World champion Damon Hill, of Britain, was eighth fastest overall on 1:47.542 in his TWR Arrows. He had a spin in the stadium complex during the wet second session but was able to continue.
The McLaren duo of Briton David Coulthard and Finn Mika Hakkinen, who are powered by German Mercedes engines, had a troubled time despite going into the event as favourites for victory.

Coulthard could only manage the 17th best time, while Hakkinen was lucky to manage the eighth quickest time despite not setting a time in the first session after he stopped out on the track with an engine problem.

"There is a lot of expectation from Mercedes here, and I am still confident that we have a car and engine package that suits the track," said Coulthard, the winner of this year's Australian Grand Prix.
